baseline_models.focus_anchor: The question of security is answered by two land-based failure modes: the ground can engulf from below, or a pebble-bearing wind can strike from above.
baseline_models.mechanism: Settled confidence treats arrival on dry land as arrival in a safe medium. The verse encloses that position vertically: the dry ground can cease to support, while what is dispatched through the air can turn the ground's own small stones into impact.

activation_trace.role: Heart-settled security supplies the confidence challenged by the opening question.
The ground's sinking turns the apparently supporting medium into the lower source of danger.
Dry land and open country name the medium mistakenly treated as categorically safe.
Dispatch and release make the upper threat an intentionally set-in-motion counterpart to sinking.
A violent wind carrying dust or pebbles supplies the overhead impact that completes the enclosure.

changed_reading.before: A warning that one of two natural disasters may occur on land.
changed_reading.after: A dismantling of medium-based security: land offers no protected vertical zone because its support can open below and its loose matter can return from above.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The threat attaches to the side or flank of the dry land rather than naming land only as an undifferentiated place.
baseline_models.mechanism: The side image can mark a bounded flank, adjacency, or protective face. Sinking that very side makes the presumed edge or shield the point of breach, so proximity to a boundary supplies no escape route.

activation_trace.role: A bodily flank or spatial side gives the land a bounded, vulnerable face.
A shield set at one's side supplies the protective expectation that the threatened flank reverses.
Dry land provides the bounded surface whose side is treated as refuge.
Ground disappearance converts the apparent protective flank into the breach itself.

changed_reading.before: The phrase merely locates a disaster somewhere on land.
changed_reading.after: The verse targets the refuge function of an edge or flank: the side relied on as a shield can itself give way.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: After the physical threat, the verse moves to not finding any wakil.
baseline_models.mechanism: The sequence closes not only routes of bodily escape but also delegated agency. Finding is active location or attainment; a wakil is one entrusted to stand over an affair with sufficiency and preservation. Once the event arrives, no substitute manager of the threatened party's affair can be located.

activation_trace.role: Finding as locating or attaining makes the closing negation an exhaustive failed search.
Entrusting an affair to another supplies the unavailable transfer of agency.
One who stands over an affair with sufficiency and preservation supplies the unavailable protective office.

changed_reading.before: No rescuer will be available after the disaster.
changed_reading.after: The warning also forecloses agency transfer: nobody can be found to take over, preserve, or answer for the threatened party's affair.

context_deltas.mechanism: The preceding sequence contrasts a promise that opens hope but deceives with a Lord whose custodianship is sufficient. The focus question then tests whether felt safety has been lodged in the deceptive promise, and its final denial of a wakil removes every rival office without denying the sufficient wakil just named.

activation_trace.role: Settled confidence is the focus state reclassified by the preceding contrast.
A spoken promise that opens hope supplies the prospective basis of false security.
Deception by what glitters but does not hold classifies that promised security as structurally unstable.
Standing over an affair until it is sufficient supplies the positive standard for real custody.
The sufficient keeper named immediately before the focus distinguishes true custodianship from an absent rival.
The same office is negated for the addressees after the threat, closing recourse to any alternative keeper.

structural_cues: 17:64 ends with deceptive promise, 17:65 names sufficient custodianship, and 17:68 ends by denying any wakil to the addressees.
The focus interrogative challenges an achieved feeling of safety rather than merely predicting fear.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies deceptive promise and sufficient divine custody; I infer that the promise can feed the felt security challenged in 17:68 and that the denied wakil is a rival office. A live alternative is that the question rebukes forgetfulness without assigning that confidence specifically to the promise.

changed_reading.before: No protector at all exists once punishment begins.
changed_reading.after: The verse distinguishes custody from counter-custody: sufficient keeping has just been located, while every deceptive or rival delegation on which the addressees might rely is made unfindable.

context_deltas.mechanism: Rescue separates the travelers from sea danger and deposits them on dry land, but the next warning makes that landing surface itself fail. The following ayah can return them to sea, dispatch a breaking wind, and drown them. The focus is therefore the hinge of a reversible transport cycle, not a declaration that one medium is safe.

activation_trace.role: Ground disappearance reverses the support apparently gained at landfall.
Escape by separation supplies the sea-to-land transition that is mistaken for final safety.
Dry land is the destination of rescue and thus the surface whose refuge status 17:68 immediately revokes.
Return after departure makes movement between danger media repeatable rather than terminal.
A second dispatch mirrors the focus dispatch and preserves one directing agency across land and sea.
Drowning supplies the sea-side counterpart to disappearance into land.

structural_cues: The ordered sequence is sea distress, rescue to land, land engulfment or stone-wind, then possible return to sea and drowning.
17:69 repeats the focus pattern of feeling secure, a dispatched threat, and then finding no relational recourse.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the ordered medium changes and repeated warning syntax; I infer that their recurrence deliberately ablates confidence in any medium. A live alternative is that 17:68 and 17:69 are parallel independent threats rather than a transport cycle.

changed_reading.before: The sea crisis is over at landfall, after which a separate land disaster is threatened.
changed_reading.after: Landfall is only relocation within a reversible field of exposure: the rescuer governs every transition, and neither shore nor sea can become an autonomous refuge.

context_deltas.mechanism: The next sequence describes humanity as honored and carried on land and sea. Read back into the focus, dry land is not property held under human control but a carrying arrangement. Engulfment reverses that relation: the carrier can cease bearing and take the carried body into itself.

activation_trace.role: The land's side becomes a bodily-like face of the carrier rather than a neutral coordinate.
Sinking ground reverses bearing into engulfment.
Bestowed honor supplies a status that can be mistaken for guaranteed immunity.
Bearing a visible load casts humans as carried rather than self-grounding.
The same dry-land medium is named as a domain of carriage, activating its support function in the focus.

structural_cues: The threat to the side of the land is followed two ayat later by explicit human carriage on land and sea.
Honor and carriage are grammatically bestowed, while the focus interrogative treats security as an unwarranted conclusion.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies bestowed honor, carriage, and the same land term; I infer a carrier-carried reversal when the ground sinks. A live alternative is that carriage on land denotes ordinary travel and does not personify or materialize the substrate.

changed_reading.before: Human standing on land is the stable default interrupted by disaster.
changed_reading.after: Standing is already a granted mode of being carried; engulfment exposes the contingency of that support, and bestowed honor does not convert carriage into immunity.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later sequence brings written determination, non-deprivation, another failed search for a helper, and an established way that admits no alteration. Those cues give the focus wakil a procedural edge: after the threat, one cannot appoint another to carry the matter, alter the governing course, or answer in one's place.

activation_trace.role: Delegating an affair to another anchors the possible procedural transfer that the verse denies.
Writing as an established judgment supplies a fixed record against which delegated escape would have to operate.
Withholding a due right supplies the explicitly excluded procedural defect.
The repeated failed finding turns the focus close into part of a recurring search-for-recourse formula.
Aid that makes another prevail supplies a distinct relational office also made unavailable.
A running, followed way supplies the governing course within which recourse is sought.
Change from one state to another supplies the alteration explicitly unavailable to a would-be representative.

structural_cues: 17:69, 17:75, and 17:77 repeat forms of not finding recourse after a consequential clause.
The unavailable roles vary across wakil, tabi, and nasir, broadening the closure from physical rescue to representation, pursuit, and aid.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies delegation, a fixed written judgment, fair treatment, repeated unavailable helpers, and an unalterable way; I infer a procedural arrow from wakil to nontransferable answerability. A live alternative is that wakil remains purely a protector and acquires no representative nuance here.

changed_reading.before: The closing phrase only says that nobody can physically protect the addressees.
changed_reading.after: The phrase also denies procedural substitution: no delegate can take over their matter, alter its governing course, or absorb their answerability.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later context makes stability an act of strengthening, leaning a reliance on a strong side, and expulsion an adversarial attempt to shake someone loose from the earth. The focus can then be heard as the vertical limit of the same support problem: not merely being driven across land, but losing the land-side on which stance depends.

activation_trace.role: Ground disappearance supplies the vertical loss of stance.
A spatial or bodily side supplies the support face exposed to failure.
Actively strengthening a thing supplies stability as conferred support rather than an inherent condition.
A strong side leaned upon supplies the social analogue of reliance on the land's side.
Lightness that shakes stability supplies the attempted loosening from place.
The lower realm opposite the sky supplies the explicit ground from which expulsion is attempted.
Passing outside a containing place supplies horizontal displacement as the comparison case.

structural_cues: 17:74 pairs bestowed stabilization with nearly leaning toward a strong side; 17:76 pairs destabilization with expulsion from the earth.
The focus places sinking beside a land-side, allowing vertical disappearance to coexist with the later horizontal displacement pattern.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies strengthening, leaning, destabilization, earth, and exit; I infer that these social and spatial relations coactivate a shared support mechanics in the focus. A live alternative is that prophetic steadfastness and threatened expulsion are independent from the geological warning.

changed_reading.before: Sinking is only a geological event.
changed_reading.after: Sinking becomes the extreme vertical form of dispossession: stability is granted, reliance has a side, and the ground itself can withdraw the stance that horizontal expulsion merely relocates.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it links the opening creation material to a later disaster across seven ayat rather than through a repeated focus lexeme. It remains anchored in the focus's sinking dry land and pebble-bearing assault, while 17:61 explicitly supplies clay as human material. Downstream prose should present it only as a contained material echo, not as a claim that clay and pebbles are lexically identical or that the verse describes bodily decomposition.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus makes earth both an engulfing substrate and the source material borne by the hāṣib.

activation_trace.role: Mixed clay supplies the material origin whose apparent inferiority begins the context and whose earth-family later becomes dangerous.
Sinking earth turns the supporting material into an engulfing medium.
Pebbles and gravel supply earth matter returned as impact.
Casting with pebbles turns inert ground material into directed assault.

changed_reading.before: The focus lists unrelated environmental weapons.
changed_reading.after: As a contained material echo, the earth-family associated with human origin and support can reverse into engulfment and stony impact, undoing confidence built on mastery of material place.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it uses the packet's non-dominant split mapping of the focus root و ج د to ج د د, so the shoreline and level-ground images are form-distant from ordinary finding. It remains packet-valid and focus-anchored at the word for finding beside the land-side construction. Downstream prose should mark it as secondary branch resonance or wordplay, never replace the ordinary sense of finding with shoreline.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The negated finding stands beside a threatened side of dry land, allowing the split branch inventory to echo the loss of an edge and level surface.

activation_trace.role: A water edge or shoreline supplies a branch-distant spatial object that cannot function as the sought refuge.
The level face of the earth supplies the stable surface erased by sinking.
The land's side anchors the distant shoreline image to an explicit spatial edge in the focus.
Dry land supplies the surface and shore-side field within which the resonance operates.

changed_reading.before: Not finding a wakil is solely a failed search for a person.
changed_reading.after: Without displacing that primary sense, the split branch inventory lets the failed finding echo a failed shore or level-ground refuge: neither a protective agent nor a stable edge can be attained.

strongest_changes: The sea-rescue, land-threat, and sea-return sequence makes 17:68 the hinge of a reversible exposure cycle rather than a separate land warning.
The contrast between deceptive promise and sufficient custody revises the absent wakil into the failure of every rival delegation, not the absence of true custody.
The later written judgment and repeated no-finding clauses give wakil a live procedural layer of nontransferable answerability.
summary.what_was_special: The focus organizes security through support relations: land is a carried-on surface with a vulnerable side, threats close from below and above, and the final failed search removes delegated agency. The packet's split و ج د inventory preserves an additional, explicitly contained shore-and-surface resonance.
remaining_uncertainties: The procedural representative force of wakil may remain subordinate to its more direct protector and keeper sense.
The stability, leaning, and expulsion sequence may be analogy rather than a deliberate activation of geological sinking.
The clay-to-pebble and split-mapping shoreline readings are valid exploratory echoes but should not control a primary rendering.
